newsitem.title: UK: HSBC gains on HK rally, ahead of results.
newsitem.headline: HSBC gains on HK rally, ahead of results.

text.p: Shares in HSBC Holdings Plc advanced on Tuesday after the stock reached an all-time high in Hong Kong ahead of the group's results next week.
The shares were up 21-1/2p at 15.85 stg by 1145 GMT amid continuing demand for banking stocks.

"There's a lot of interest in the banks at the moment," said one trader. "Compared with the likes of NatWest and Barclays, HSBC's strategy of going for the retail market seems to offer better value," said another.

The shares reached an all-time high of HK$194.00 earlier in Hong Kong, buoyed by expectations of strong results from the group on Monday and as the Hang Seng put in a strong performance to close more than one percent higher.
The gains came despite a report in the Financial Times on Tuesday which highlighted the widening price gap between the Hong Kong dollar and sterling denominated shares.
The sterling denominated shares were quoted at a 48p premium to the Hong Kong dollar denominated stock despite the shares carrying the same benefits.
"It is usual for the (sterling denominated) shares to be trading at a premium, though historically that premium has been around 30p," the trader said.
The FT noted that this differential was now the widest seen since 1993.
"The major turnover is seen in the sterling stock and as long as this level of demand continues I can't see the current premium narrowing," said the trader.
"The only people that can justify this differential are the fund managers that pay the premium, they seem to prefer having a sterling denominated stock within their portfolio."
